rationale: hammernik_2017-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_filter_init_std=0.05, vn_rbf_init_std=0.01, vn_lambda_init=0.02, epochs=20, batch_size=2, lr=0.00096, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, max_train_s=1500, rationale=iter-9 (six-box). AXES so far (best=iter-6 T=5,f=16,k=9,lambda=0.02,lr=9.6e-4, hr=0.6329): lambda optimum=0.02 (0.05 collapsed); depth T 3->4->5 helps (decelerating, T=5 best, budget-capped ep<=20); width f=16->24 REGRESSED (iter-7 0.5227); lr 9.6e-4->5e-4 REGRESSED (iter-8 0.5196, under-converges). lr and width exhausted. UNTESTED productive lever: receptive field. ONE KNOB vs iter-6: vn_kernel 9 -> 11 (larger analysis filters; paper's near-best k). HYPOTHESIS: sparse-view streaks are long-range; a wider kernel lets each filter capture them better, lifting hr above 0.6329; if it regresses, k=9 was sufficient or larger kernels over-smooth. All else = iter-6 (T=5, f=16, n_bumps=31, x_range=2.0, lambda=0.02, lr=9.6e-4, batch=2, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, train_n=400) with ep=20/max_train_s=1500 (the budget-safe T=5 setting proven by iter-8-rerun at 1622s). k=11 ~1.5x conv cost but the RBF-bump loop dominates wall, so modest increase -> stays under the 1800s kill. batch_size=2 (OOM guard); expandable_segments via --export.
